comment: Connector registry. The Node builder reads this to (a) render connector signatures into the generation prompt, (b) copy the right template files into a generated project, (c) build .env.example from required_env, and (d) build a deployed image's dependency list from pip_requires. Keep in sync with the .py files — tool_templates/__init__.py has a check_catalog() that verifies it.
auth_comment: How a workspace supplies this connector's credential. `oauth` means Jaroku owns the OAuth app and the user grants it access by clicking Connect — the value reaching a run is a short-lived access token the control plane minted, and `required_env` still lists the names a HAND-CONFIGURED install uses, because an exported project has no Jaroku to ask. `user_secret` means the user supplies the value themselves and it goes into the vault under those exact names. `none` means the connector needs no credential at all. The field decides what the connections panel offers, what .env.example says about each key, and what the generation prompt tells the model about where a credential comes from.
pip_requires_comment: The PyPI requirements each connector's template lazy-imports, as they appear in runtime/pyproject.toml's `connectors` extra. Split per connector because a deployed image should install what its agent actually uses, not the union — an agent with one Postgres tool has no business pulling in the Google API client. check_catalog() proves every entry is still a subset of the extra, so the two cannot drift.

connectors.label: Gmail
connectors.description: Search the user's mail and create draft replies. Creates drafts only — never sends.

tools.name: gmail_search
tools.summary: Search Gmail using Gmail search syntax (e.g. 'from:acme.com is:unread'). Returns sender, subject and snippet per match.

tools.name: gmail_create_draft
tools.signature: gmail_create_draft(to: str, subject: str, body: str, reply_to_message_id: str = '') -> str
tools.summary: Create a draft reply. Does NOT send. Pass reply_to_message_id to thread onto an existing conversation.

connectors.label: Slack
connectors.description: List and read public channels, and post messages. Posting is immediate and cannot be undone.

tools.name: slack_list_channels
tools.summary: List public channels the bot can see, with ids and member counts.

tools.name: slack_read_channel
tools.summary: Read recent messages from a channel by name or id.

tools.name: slack_post_message
tools.summary: Post a message to a channel. Irreversible — use only when the user asked for a message to be sent.

connectors.label: Postgres
connectors.description: Read-only SQL access. Writes and DDL are rejected by both a statement check and a read-only transaction.

tools.name: pg_query
tools.summary: Run ONE read-only SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT) and return rows, capped at 100. Writes, DDL and multi-statement input are rejected.
